newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin to hold more talks with Chirac on cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Jospin to hold more talks with Chirac on cabinet.

text.p: Socialist French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin will hold a second meeting with conservative President Jacques Chirac on Wednesday to discuss the formation of a left-wing cabinet, the president's office said.

It was not immediately clear whether they had failed to agree on the full cabinet list at a first one-hour meeting earlier in the afternoon, or whether the second session was just to complete the list.

The president has to approve the appointment of ministers and the new government is traditionally announced by the secretary-general of the president's office on the steps of the Elysee presidential palace.
Socialist party sources said that at their first meeting, Jospin discussed with Chirac the most "sensitive ministries", including foreign affairs and defence, interior and justice.
The prime minister said afterwards the talks had gone "very well" but did not say when the cabinet would be announced.

Close Jospin associate Dominique Strauss-Kahn, author of the Socialists' economic programme, was expected to be named finance minister, and former labour minister Martine Aubry would get a super-ministry of employment and social affairs, they said.
